run.procedureSummary: Step 1, Feed: add that cycle's feed row to each chamber, 1 to 6. Chambers may go over their holding limit. Step 2, Carry forward: go through chambers 1 to 6 in turn. If a chamber is over its holding limit, set it to the limit and add the excess to the next chamber, so excess can cascade within the same pass. Chamber 6's excess goes to the loss tally. Step 3, State check, using the masses after carry forward: a LARVAL chamber at or above its upper mark becomes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber at or below its lower mark becomes LARVAL. Otherwise the state stays the same. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, before, after). Step 4, Metabolism: all amounts are worked out from the post-carry masses before anything moves, then applied together. A LARVAL chamber loses floor(m/4) to the tally. A PUPAL chamber gives floor(m/2) to the chamber before it (i-1); chamber 1's amount goes to the tally. Mass over the limit stays where it is until the next cycle's carry forward, and none follows cycle 5. Step 5, Moult: if the line total is strictly greater than 38, every chamber becomes floor(m/2), the removed mass goes to the tally, and the cycle is logged.

openPoints.assumption: Chambers are processed one after another, 1 to 6. Excess passed into chamber i+1 counts toward that chamber's own overflow check in the same pass. For example, in cycle 1 chamber 2's excess of 4 pushed chamber 3 to 13, and chamber 3 then passed 1 to chamber 4.

openPoints.point: Which mass the state check and metabolism use
openPoints.assumption: The state check uses the masses after carry forward. Metabolism uses the states just set in this cycle's state check and the same post-carry masses.
'Over 38' means strictly greater than 38. Cycle 5 ended at exactly 38, so no moult fired that cycle.

openPoints.point: Moult rounding and where the mass goes
openPoints.assumption: Each chamber is floored separately (m//2). The removed amount, m - floor(m/2) summed over all chambers, goes to the tally, including the extra unit lost from odd masses.
Rounding is down for each chamber separately: floor(m/4) for LARVAL and floor(m/2) for PUPAL. Chamber 1's PUPAL reabsorption goes to the tally.

openPoints.point: State check is a single comparison
openPoints.assumption: Each chamber can change state at most once per cycle. A chamber that becomes PUPAL is not checked again against its lower mark in the same step.

No carry forward follows cycle 5, so the end masses are reported as they are after metabolism and the moult check. Chambers 2 and 4 end above their holding limits (10 > 8 and 7 > 6), as the write-up allows.

run.balanceCheck: Starting total 20 + all feed 94 = 114. End total 38 (6+10+9+7+4+2) + loss tally 76 = 114. The two sides match.
